Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Financial Corp. Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, during the Q&A session, please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. This event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Financial Corp.'s results for the third quarter. With me this morning are Johnathan Reeves, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer; David Wong, Chief Credit Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Operating Officer; Amanda Torres, Chief Marketing Officer; and Gregory Hale, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Reeves.

Johnathan Reeves:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Financial Corp. delivered record results in the third quarter, exceeding all previous benchmarks and solidifying our position as a leader in the financial services industry.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on sustaining strong revenue growth, driving operational efficiency, managing risk effectively, investing in technology and innovation, enhancing customer experience, strengthening our brand reputation, promoting a diverse and inclusive culture, and delivering superior returns to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on our net interest income trends showing solid year-over-year growth; deposit growth across transactional, savings, and time categories with strategic retention efforts; provision for credit losses managed through rigorous CECL modeling; asset sensitivity positioned for rate resilience; impact of market conditions bolstering non-interest income; revenue diversification reducing cyclicality; key strategic initiatives advancing digital and regional expansion; and forward earnings guidance reflecting disciplined growth.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. UniBank Financial Corp. reported net income of $1.5 billion for the third quarter, or $1.92 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 6% year-over-year, driven by growth in our loan portfolio and improved net interest margin. Non-interest income saw robust performance reflecting diversification across investment banking, wealth management, and fees. We are generating strong returns on equity and are committed to delivering value to our shareholders.

Good morning, everyone. Before we move to other updates, let me dive deeper into our net interest income performance and provide forward guidance for the fourth quarter. NII remains the bedrock of our P&L here at UniBank, representing over 65% of our total revenue this quarter, and we're pleased with the trajectory amid a still-resilient but normalizing rate environment.

For the quarter just ended, Q3 NII came in at $2.52 billion, up 6% year-over-year and 2% quarter-over-quarter. This beat our whisper number by about $25 million, driven primarily by a 10 basis point expansion in our net interest margin to 3.48%. On the asset side, average earning assets grew 3% year-over-year to $285 billion, fueled by solid loan portfolio expansion. Commercial and industrial loans—our highest-yielding bucket at 6.2% yield—grew 5% annualized, benefiting from drawdowns in our revolving lines to middle-market clients in the manufacturing and tech sectors. Consumer lending held steady with 2% growth, anchored by our auto and credit card portfolios, where yields averaged 5.8%. We did see some moderation in mortgage originations due to sticky 30-year rates hovering around 6.8%, but our held-for-investment jumbo pipeline remains robust at $4.2 billion, yielding 4.9%.

A key tailwind was our proactive asset-liability management. We've been rotating lower-duration securities into higher-yielding floating-rate notes and private credit allocations, boosting overall portfolio yield by 15 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 5.45%. Our private credit platform, in partnership with firms similar to Ares Management, now totals $12 billion in commitments, with realizations yielding 8-10% net IRR, helping offset any drag from our $45 billion AFS securities portfolio, which saw $150 million in unrealized losses due to the recent 25 basis point Fed cut in September.

Shifting to the liability side, funding costs rose modestly to 1.97%, a 5 basis point increase quarter-over-quarter, reflecting deposit betas normalizing at around 45% for non-interest-bearing DDA accounts. Total deposits grew 1% quarter-over-quarter to $240 billion, with low-cost core deposits at 72% of the mix. We faced stiff competition from money market funds offering 5%+ APYs—like Vanguard's VMFXX sucking up retail liquidity—but our relationship-driven franchise held firm. In the Southeast U.S., where we have 25% market share in community banking, we grew deposits 4% via targeted promotions on our high-yield savings linked to our UniDigital app. Conversely, in Europe, our wholesale funding costs ticked up 10 basis points due to ECB policy divergence, but our €15 billion Euro-denominated deposits remain sticky at 1.5% cost.

Strategically, we've leaned into tech initiatives to defend and grow NII. Our new AI-powered dynamic pricing engine for deposits—rolled out in July across 80% of branches—has improved beta management by optimizing rates in real-time based on customer tenure and cross-sell propensity, capturing 200 basis points more in wallet share from fintech challengers like SoFi and Ally. On the lending side, our embedded finance platform with QuickBooks integration drove 15% growth in SMB loan originations, with seamless API pulls reducing underwriting time to under 24 hours.

Now, turning to Q4 guidance. We expect NII of $2.58 billion to $2.62 billion, implying 2-4% sequential growth and a NIM range of 3.50% to 3.55%. This assumes two additional 25 basis point Fed cuts in November and December, bringing the funds rate to 4.50-4.75%, with deposit betas peaking at 50% before stabilizing. Loan growth should moderate to 3% annualized, with caution around office CRE—we're keeping exposure under 2% of loans and provisioning conservatively at 45 basis points—while pivoting to multifamily and industrial, where cap rates are compressing to 5.5%.

On the broader earnings picture, we guide adjusted EPS to $1.88 to $1.96, up 8% year-over-year at the midpoint. This incorporates non-interest revenue of $1.45 billion (flat quarter-over-quarter, with fee income from capital markets rebounding 10% on M&A advisory), expenses at $2.1 billion (up 2% due to FDIC assessment tailwinds fading but offset by $50 million in efficiency savings from our GenAI back-office automation), and a provision for credit losses of $300 million (15 basis points of loans, reflecting CRE normalization but pristine consumer delinquencies at 1.2%). Our CET1 ratio remains fortress-like at 11.8%, giving us ample dry powder for buybacks—we've authorized $2 billion remaining under our program.

Regionally, U.S. operations should contribute 75% of NII growth, with strength in Texas energy lending (yields up to SOFR + 250 basis points) and Florida wealth management cross-sell, where AUM grew 12%. In Asia-Pacific, our joint venture with DBS Bank is ramping private banking fees, but we're tempering expansion amid China's property sector headwinds. Europe remains a margin drag short-term due to negative carry on excess HQLA, but our stress-tested LCR of 125% positions us well.

Let me now turn to our provision for credit losses, which came in at $450 million for the quarter, bringing the full-year total toward conservative levels reflective of our disciplined CECL methodology and proactive portfolio management amid a resilient yet uncertain macroeconomic backdrop. Our net charge-offs for the quarter were $320 million, or 45 basis points of average loans and leases, up modestly from prior periods but stable year-over-year. Delinquency rates across the portfolio ticked up to 1.8%, driven primarily by commercial and industrial segments, but remain well below pandemic peaks.

We calculate provisions across our $450 billion loan portfolio using a probability of default, loss given default, and exposure at default model suite, calibrated quarterly with overlays for macroeconomic scenarios. Our PD models incorporate over 200 vintage cohorts segmented by product, geography, and borrower characteristics—FICO scores for consumers, debt service coverage ratios above 1.25x for CRE, and EBITDA multiples under 6x for leveraged C&I deals. Key enhancements this year include our rollout of machine learning-driven PD forecasting in partnership with Moody's Analytics, reducing model uncertainty by 18% and improving capture of nonlinear effects from variables like CME FedWatch Tool probabilities.

We've stress-tested against baseline, adverse, and severe scenarios, feeding into our allowance for credit losses of $14.7 billion—a coverage ratio of 3.25% of loans, providing robust cushioning at 2.1x projected two-year net charge-offs. Breaking down drivers: Consumer lending contributed $180 million, with auto delinquencies at 2.1%; CRE $210 million, with office challenges prompting derisking of $2.5 billion; C&I $50 million amid yield curve pressures; and international minimal at $10 million. Macro overlays added $75 million incorporating downside risks from Fed funds, inflation, and recession probabilities.

Strategically, we're diversifying portfolios, upgrading tech stacks with Palantir for real-time simulations, and maintaining disciplined origination with improved risk ratings. We expect Q1 PCL in the $400-475 million range.

On deposit growth and mix, our franchise remains the bedrock of our balance sheet, driving our 3.45% NIM. Deposits grew 9.2% year-over-year to $262.4 billion, outpacing industry averages. Core deposits—transactional and savings excluding brokered—comprise 82%. Transactional deposits at $118.1 billion (45%) grew 4.7% YoY with low betas; savings at $91.7 billion (35%) accelerated 12.5% via competitive APYs and digital channels; time deposits at $52.6 billion (20%) surged 18.3% but managed with cost discipline.

Trends show rotation to yield-chasing but stabilizing uninsured ratios at 28%. Regionally, Southeast led with 13% growth, Asia-Pacific 15%. Strategies include loyalty programs boosting cross-sell to 3.8x, UniWallet Pro for inflows, and AI personalization for upsells. We expect Q4 growth of 7-9%.

Regarding the impact of market conditions on non-interest income, which totaled $2.8 billion, up 7% YoY and 28% of revenue, resilience shines amid inflation, rate cut pricing, and geopolitics. CIB fees at $1.1 billion mixed with M&A dips but equity underwriting surges; trading $650 million on VIX spikes; CCB $520 million from consumer spending; AWM $530 million with alternatives momentum. Initiatives like AlphaFlow and embedded finance mitigate headwinds. We expect 5-8% Q4 growth.

Our revenue diversification initiatives have elevated non-interest to 42% of revenue, offsetting NII softness and driving 8% total growth. Wealth management fees up 22% to $1.8 billion on $25 billion inflows and GlobalWealth AI; transaction banking 28% to $1.1 billion via GlobalPayLink and blockchain; CIB 15% rebound. Impacts include stronger RoTE, lower volatility, targeting 45% mix by 2025.

Finally, on NII trends more broadly, Q3 NII at $14.8 billion up 4.2% YoY but down 1.8% QoQ, with NIM at 3.45%. Consumer, C&I, and global markets drove YoY gains; regions varied with APAC strong. Initiatives like deposit optimization and hedging stabilize outlook.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate risk, credit risk, operational risk, and geopolitical exposures. On asset sensitivity and interest rate risk management, our modestly asset-sensitive profile has driven NII tailwinds in this higher-for-longer environment. A +100 bps shock accretes NII by $185 million; -100 bps a -$112 million headwind. EVE sensitivity well within limits. We've hedged with $4.2 billion swaps, reducing duration gap, and enhanced ALM with AI platforms. Regionally positioned strong, targeting 3-5% sensitivity.

We are implementing enhanced controls and monitoring to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile.

David Wong:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains excellent with non-performing loans at 0.85% and net charge-offs at 0.35%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are leveraging technology to enhance customer experience, improve efficiency, and drive innovation. Our investments in AI-driven platforms and cloud-native architectures like Apex One are yielding significant results, with digital users up 32% and fraud detection at 99.7% accuracy.

Robert Kline:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include streamlining our processes, optimizing our infrastructure, and leveraging data analytics to improve decision-making.

Amanda Torres:
Thank you. From a marketing perspective, we are focused on strengthening our brand reputation and enhancing customer engagement. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly successful in driving customer acquisition and retention.

Gregory Hale:
Good morning. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of compliance and ethical conduct. We are continuously strengthening our compliance programs and working closely with regulators to ensure we are meeting all applicable requirements.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Could you please provide more detail on your key strategic initiatives and progress?

Johnathan Reeves:
Thanks, John. Our strategy is anchored in digital transformation, revenue diversification, and regional expansion. We've rolled out next-gen mobile banking on AWS with Google Cloud, driving 32% growth in digital users to 14.2 million and 45% surge in mobile deposits. AI fraud detection has safeguarded billions, while wealth AUM grew 19% to $450 billion via robo-advisors. Payments volume up 27%, sustainable finance book 52% larger at $15 billion. Regionally, U.S. deposits up 11%, Europe commercial revenue 24%, Asia-Pacific 41%. CET1 at 13.2%, on track for 12-14% EPS growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
What is your outlook for NII and earnings in the coming quarter?

Michael Chen:
Emily, as detailed, Q4 NII guidance is $2.58 to $2.62 billion with NIM 3.50-3.55%, assuming Fed cuts. EPS $1.88-$1.96, incorporating stable non-interest revenue, controlled expenses, and $300 million provisions. CET1 supports buybacks, with U.S. leading growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Robert Lee:
Can you discuss the impact of interest rate changes and your asset sensitivity?

Lisa Patel:
Absolutely, Robert. We're asset-sensitive with +4.2% NII uplift on +100 bps shock. Hedging via swaps and swaptions has optimized duration to +0.70 years. Tech like Murex AI enhances forecasting, positioning us for cuts with maintained sensitivity.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Susan Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Susan Kim:
What are your plans for technology investments amid strategic initiatives?

Elena Vasquez:
Susan, we're prioritizing AI and cloud for 75% digital interactions by year-end. Platforms like Apex Shield and open banking APIs have boosted acquisition 15%, with cybersecurity zero-trust reducing threats 55%. These de-risk while compounding returns.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Reeves for any closing remarks.

Johnathan Reeves:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Financial Corp. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
